- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots downward; apply a “lag correction” — delay downward trend by 1–3 periods unless sentiment shifts to negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price drops sharply, model underestimates further decline; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; use 1–2% smoothing filter to dampen extreme swings.
- If true outcome shows “rebound after dip” (e.g., drop then rise), model often misses the rebound; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias in next period if sentiment turns positive.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, avoid linear extrapolation — always check if sentiment or event context (e.g., policy change, ETS auction) overrides trend.
